Volume One.
1. The First Assembly on the Expedient Means of Making Offerings. Homage to the Dharmakāya, perfectly pure and complete, to Vairocana, the Wisdom that Shines Everywhere!
The eye of wondrous enlightenment is fully blossomed, Broad and expansive like the petals of a blue lotus.
Now, relying on the essentials of the sūtras, I shall briefly explain The methods for attaining the *siddhi* of self-benefit and benefit for others,
The sequential application of mantras and skillful means, And the sublime gateway for engendering faith and understanding.
First, cause one’s own mind to be free from dust and defilement;
contemplate all Buddhas appearing before you, and clearly visualize yourself situated within their presence.
With devotion, scatter exquisite incense and flowers, along with various supreme and wondrous ornaments; gaze upon the deity, the vidyā-mantra, and the mudrā.
With single-minded reverence, perform the prostration.
The expedient mantra for prostrating is:
Oṃ namas sarvatathāgatānāṃ kāyavākcittānāṃ vajranamane karomi. By means of this true mantra of prostration, one is able to prostrate universally to the Buddhas of the ten directions!
With my right knee touching the ground and palms joined, I contemplate and confess my past sinful karma.
Through ignorance, I have accumulated various offenses of body, speech, and mind;
because greed, hatred, and delusion shrouded my heart, [I failed] toward the Buddha, the True Dharma, and the Noble Sangha!
Toward my parents, the two teachers, spiritual friends, and all immeasurable sentient beings,
throughout the beginningless cycle of birth and death, I have committed extremely grave and inexhaustible sins; now,
in the presence of the Buddhas of the ten directions currently living!
I confess all [misdeeds] and shall not commit them again.
Oṃ sarva-pāpa-śodhaya nātha-vajraya svāhā. Homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time!
The three kinds of eternal bodies, the treasury of the True Dharma, And the assembly of those with the great mind of supreme vows and bodhicitta— I now take refuge in all of them completely.
The mantra of the skillful means for taking refuge says:
"I purify this body, freeing it from all defilements, As well as the body, speech, and mind of the three periods of time."
Exceeding the number of atoms in oceans of lands, I offer them to all the Tathāgatas!
The mantra for the skillful means of offering the body says:
The jewel of the supreme vow of the pure bodhicitta, I now arouse it to deliver all sentient beings.
Enveloped by the accumulation of the suffering of birth and other afflictions, and bodies harmed by ignorance—
may you rescue, gather, and provide refuge for them to bring about liberation, and always benefit all sentient beings.
The Expedient Mantra for Generating the Bodhicitta is:
Oṃ, *bhūricintā*, *mudrapadānaye*. O ocean-like assembly of all the Perfectly Enlightened Ones throughout the infinite worlds of the ten directions!
Through the power of various skillful means, and by all the sons of the Buddhas for the sake of sentient beings—
whatever meritorious deeds they have cultivated— I now rejoice in them all.
The mantra for the skillful means of sympathetic joy (*anumodana*) is:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatapraṇidhānābhyudgata-megha-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. I now entreat all the Tathāgatas, the world-saviors whose great resolve is for awakening!
I only pray that throughout the realms of the ten directions, you will always let fall the rain of Dharma from great clouds.
The mantra for the exhortation of skillful means says:
May those dwelling as ordinary beings quickly cast off this body, which is a collection of manifold sufferings.
When one attains the stainless state, One dwells securely in the body of the pure Dharma-realm.
The mantra for the skillful means of the Dharma-body is as follows:
"Whatever wholesome karmas have been cultivated, For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings,"
I now dedicate all of this correctly, To eliminate the suffering of birth and death and reach Bodhi.
The Mantra for the Skillful Means of Dedication says:
In order to make body and mind universally pure, And out of compassion to rescue and protect oneself and others.
The nature of the mind is thus free from all defilements.
Clearly and attentively contemplate the first letter-gateway: a white, empty circle with nine concentric rims.
Next, one should bind the *samaya* mudrā, which is said to purify the three paths of action.
One should follow the characteristics of the secret mudrā as taught by all the Samyaksaṃbuddhas:
one should join the hands of concentration and wisdom, erect the two wheels of emptiness,
touch all the limbs of the body, and recite the words of truth.
The mantra for purifying the three paths of action is as follows:
By merely forming this seal, one can purify the ground of the Tathāgatas;
the pāramitā of the ground is fulfilled, and the realm of the path of the Three Dharmas is accomplished.
Regarding the various mudrās and so forth, as explained in succession,
the mantrin should know that whatever is performed will attain accomplishment.
Next, one binds the Dharmadhātusaṃbhava, the emblem of secret wisdom.
Because of purifying body, speech, and mind, one universally manifests emanated bodies.
With the hands of Prajñā and Samādhi, both form vajra-fists;
the two "emptinesses" rest upon the palms, and the wind-banner is held perfectly upright.
This is called the Dharma-realm, the secret seal of purity.
The mantra for generating the Dharma-realm is as follows:
"Just as the self-nature of the Dharma-realm, so one should contemplate one's own body."
Or by means of true speech, it is proclaimed through three turnings.
One should see that which abides in the essence of phenomena, stainless like space;
for, through the power of mantras and mudrās, the practitioner is empowered.
To cause that [realization] to become firm, one contemplates one’s own vajra body and binds the Vajrajñāna-mudrā,
correctly visualizing the hands with palms facing away from each other.
The wheels of earth, water, fire, and wind are held by the left and right hands respectively.
Rotate the two empty [hands] individually, then join them within the palms of wisdom;
this is called the Dharma-Wheel Seal, the most supreme and auspicious mudrā.
Such a person shall, before long, become equal to the Savior of the World.
Through the power of mantra and mudrā, the siddha shall behold [the truth] and,
constantly revolving according to reality, turn the Great Wheel of Dharma.
The mantra of the Vajrasattva-cakra is as follows:
Having recited this mantra, one should abide in meditative equipoise and clearly contemplate that this body of mine is indeed Vajrapāṇi!
All the countless celestial Māras and others who behold it—
Like Vajrasattva, do not give rise to a doubting mind.
Next, with mantra and mudrā, don the vajra armor;
one should visualize that the garment being worn emits flames from every part of the body.
Because one adorns the body with this, all Māras who act as obstacles, as well as other classes of evil-minded beings, shall scatter in the four directions upon seeing it.
Regarding the characteristics of the secret mudrā therein: first perform the *tripuṭa* [three-pointed] gesture.
Visualize two wind-wheels in the mind, entwined and supporting a fire-wheel above.
Two empty spaces stand side by side within the palms;
having recited that mantra, one should visualize the stainless syllable.
The mantra of the Vajra Armor is as follows:
The syllable *ra* is brilliant white, adorned with a bindu;
like a luminous jewel in a topknot, it is placed upon the crown of the head.
Even the many stains of sin accumulated throughout a hundred kalpas shall be entirely extinguished by this,
and both merit and wisdom will be fully perfected.
The mantra for this is used together with the Universal Seal (Puyin):
The mantra is identical to the Dharma-realm; immeasurable multitudes of sins are eliminated.
Before long, one shall achieve accomplishment and abide on the stage of non-retrogression.
In all places defiled by contact, one should apply this gateway of syllables.
Red in color and endowed with majestic radiance, with a wreath of flames encircling him entirely, he awakens the Earth Goddess; one should recite this verse.
Kneeling with both knees on the ground, holding the vajra firmly at the heart, and extending the five fingers of the right hand with the palm flat against the earth.
*Tvaṃ*, you; *ani-vi*, O Earth-goddess; *sākṣa*, having a feminine voice; *rakṣa*, protect!
Bhūtasaṃkṣobha-sarvabuddhān;
there is a plural sense [to the word "buddha"].
*Namo* (pronounced *tā-yi-nam*), meaning "homage" (*namas*); *li-duo-ye* (pronounced *li-do-ya*), meaning "guide" (*nāyaka*);
*zuo-li-ye* (pronounced *jo-ri-ya*), meaning "to go" (*gati*) or "to practice" (*caryā*).
Vīrya-āveśa-saṃkramaṇa-trivaiśeṣika-kula-madhu-viśuddha-bhūmi-prabheda-paramitā.
The swift ones are the four Māras,
including the celestial Māra,
who immediately manifest their armies.
Tathāgatagarbha, Pañcaskandha, Śākya.

"O you who are the close protectors of the gods, toward the Buddhas, the Teachers!"
Practicing the supreme conduct, The pure grounds and the pāramitās—

Chapter Two: The Secret Maṇḍala Rite of the Bodhi-Flag Mudrā and Emblem from the Mahāvairocana-abhisambodhi-vikurvaṇādhiṣṭhāna Sūtra. At that time, the World-Honored One further proclaimed the udāna for the rite of entering the secret maṇḍala, saying:
“The Mantra Omniscient One, Having mastered the secret maṇḍala, Acts for the disciple according to the Dharma, Completely incinerating all sins.”
When the life-span is entirely incinerated, it is rendered such that it shall not arise again;
once it has become like ashes, that life-span returns once more.
This is because by burning the syllable with the syllable, it is born anew through the syllable.
All life and birth are pure and entirely stainless.
By means of the twelve links of existence, they serve as the vessel for that;
such is the samaya of all the Tathāgatas.
The Bodhisattvas who save the world, as well as the assembly of the Buddha’s śrāvakas and all those in the world, are equal and not in opposition.
Understanding this vow of equality, [one enters] the secret maṇḍala.
Entering the teachings of all dharmas, one attains mastery over all maṇḍalas.
My body is equal to theirs, and the mantra practitioner is likewise;
because there is no difference between them, it is called the samaya.
Visualize before you the syllable "Ra," A wreath of pure radiant flames,
brilliant as the morning sun.
It can eliminate all obstacles And liberate one from the defilements of the three poisons.
So too are all phenomena. Furthermore,
he purifies the site of the path of practice, completely eliminating all faults and afflictions,
its nature being like empty space.
Just as that which is held by Vajra, so too is this ground.
By adding the syllables of the five limbs and visualizing them in meditative equipoise,
one becomes identical to the Honored Muni!
Visualizing it as the color of vajra, one empowers the lower body;
this is called the yoga seat.
Within a mass of mist, one empowers the area below one's navel.
This is called the Water of Great Compassion.
The syllable *raṃ* is like the first rays of the sun; it is red and resides within a triangle.
When empowered at the position of the heart-center, this is called the Fire of Wisdom.
Black at the wind-mandala, empowered at the limit of the white tuft of hair,
it is called the power of mastery (*vaśitā*).
Visualizing all forms as accomplished, it is empowered upon the crown of the head.
Therefore it is named "Great Emptiness.
With these five syllables adorning the body, its majestic power blazes like a torch, extinguishing all karmic offenses.
Even those Māras who act as obstacles, upon seeing this brilliant Vajra, [are subdued].

Because they have thus adorned their bodies, as they traverse through the cycle of birth and death,
they stand at the great assemblies of the Tathāgatas, marked by the banner of Bodhi;
O devas, nāgas, and yakṣas!
Receiving the teachings with reverence,
one first attains the Buddha-samādhi of the Seal,
as well as the Dharma-realm and the Wheel of Dharma.
Join the *kṣika* mudrā in homage; bend the wind-wheel (*vāyu-maṇḍala*) over the space-wheel (*ākāśa-maṇḍala*).
Join the palms hollow for the Dharma-conch; twist the wind-wheel above the space-wheel.
This is the auspicious lotus of aspiration.
The seal of the Great Vajra Wisdom;
the crown of the Mahā-tathāgata;
from the tuft of hair between the brows, it is concealed within the summit.
The mudrā of the yogin holding the alms-bowl:
the hand of wisdom is extended upward, called the "Fearless Bestowal";
hanging downward, it fulfills all wishes with compassion.
The Fist of Wisdom extends the fire and water; the wise one becomes Buddha after Buddha.
Bind the inner wind-wheel with the cord;
extend the fire-wheel with the heart-seal.
The navel of the Tathāgata Śuśuddhika is the inner binding of the water of pure wisdom; this is called the waist of the Tathāgata.
One should practice it according to the mantra.

Universal light conforms to the great boundary; the two spaces contract and enter the moon.
Wind expands like the emission of light; the contraction of fire is like the shape of a hook.
The Tathāgata’s armor is as before.
The tongue and the mark [of the ūrṇā-kośa] enter the two voids.

The "Tusk Seal" (Dantamudrā): With the winds entering the palms, recite *phaṭ* three times.
Distinguish the two wind-wheels (*vāyu-maṇḍala*) and place them upon the head of the third joint of fire; do not let them touch.
Join the lotuses of the ten powers (*daśabala*), with earth and space bent inward; the joints within the palms are joined together.
The *smṛtyupasthāna* wind pinches the space;
the *avabodha* wind holds the water.
The *samantabhadra* wish-fulfilling jewel; the lotus-closing wind adds fire.
Maitreya, having authorized the previous [mudrā], bends the wind and fire wheels downward.
Following the verse on the power of being incapable of being harmed:
"Purify the Buddha-fields and serve all Tathāgatas!"
Contemplate the ocean of fragrant water.
The mantra of the Great Ocean is:
Oṃ vimarūnadi hūṃ. "With the wondrous king of lotuses, hold the Flower Treasury World."
The assembly of the Primordial Perfectly Awakened Ones and others, having laid out the maṇḍala—
the secret within secrets, born from the womb of great compassion—
as well as the worldly and supramundane maṇḍalas throughout immeasurable worlds.
Listen now as I describe in sequence all the images therein:
Surrounded on all four sides, with a single gate and passageways,
Adorned everywhere with vajra seals, and in the center, the Karma-vajra.
Upon it is a great lotus, with a wondrous-colored vajra stem;
it has eight petals complete with filaments and anthers, naturally adorned with various jewels;
it is in full bloom, containing its fruit; within that great lotus seal—
Adorned with the point of great emptiness,
throughout the universal flower pedestal, immeasurable light constantly radiates,
surrounded by hundreds of thousands of lotus assemblies.
The lion throne of the Great Awakened One, adorned with the finest of jewels,
is situated within a great palace.
It is surrounded on all sides by various banners and canopies, interlaced with strings of pearls and other ornaments.
Exquisite jewel robes hang down,
along with clouds of various gems; a rain of diverse flowers falls everywhere,
scattering profusely to adorn the ground.
And playing various musical sounds, one should visualize within the palace pure and wondrous things:
the auspicious vase and the argha-offering.
One illuminates them with mani-lamps; this is the stage of samādhi and dhāraṇī.
The sovereign ladies-in-waiting— perfections such as those of the Buddha,
the exquisite flowers of the adornments of enlightenment, and skillful means manifesting as various performances—
sing the sounds of the wondrous Dharma to make offerings to all Tathāgatas!
By the power of my merit, The power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment,
And the power of the Dharma-realm, I abide in universal offering through the Universal Seal.
Form the seal of the Great Cakra-maṇḍala.
